C03 and C15 share the tax-refund/private-relief discrimination framework, but not the distinctive liquidation-election mechanism.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"as a stockholder in a corporation liquidated pursuant to a plan of complete liquidation, might have elected to receive. Such election, under existing law, must be made ... within 30 days after adoption of the liquidation plan.","parent_excerpt":"sole stockholders of Queens Syndicate, Incorporated, which was liquidated pursuant to a plan of complete liquidation ... the elections ... would be considered to have been filed within thirty days after the date of adoption of such plan.","explanation":"Both directives use the same specialized tax mechanism: a complete corporate liquidation coupled with a shareholder election due within 30 days of adopting the plan."},{"child_excerpt":"Mrs. Gregg ... did not make an election within the specified 30 day period.","parent_excerpt":"the filing of the elections was delayed for more than six weeks after the 30-day period prescribed by law","explanation":"The operative defect in each case is an untimely liquidation-related tax election."},{"child_excerpt":"such special relief would constitute an inequitable discrimination against other taxpayers similarly situated","parent_excerpt":"The granting of special relief in this case would constitute an unfair discrimination against other taxpayers similarly situated","explanation":"The concluding rationale is nearly identical and applies the same anti-discrimination principle to the same specialized tax-election problem."}]}
